title: Population Data and Ecosystem Stability Core Test
description: Interpret population graphs, resource limits, food-web ripple effects, and ecosystem stability.

questions.prompt: What is a population?
questions.questionText: What is a population?
options: members of the same species living in the same area
all nonliving parts of an ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: members of the same species living in the same area
questions.explanation: A population is one species in a defined area.

questions.prompt: A pond has limited nesting space. Which interaction may increase?
questions.questionText: A pond has limited nesting space. Which interaction may increase?
questions.correctAnswer: competition
questions.explanation: Limited resources can increase competition.

questions.prompt: Which data best shows a population trend?
questions.questionText: Which data best shows a population trend?
options: deer count each year for ten years
questions.correctAnswer: deer count each year for ten years
questions.explanation: Counts over time can show a trend.

questions.prompt: A food web shows grass -> rabbits -> foxes. If grass decreases after drought, what may happen first?
questions.questionText: A food web shows grass -> rabbits -> foxes. If grass decreases after drought, what may happen first?
options: rabbits may have less food available
questions.correctAnswer: rabbits may have less food available
questions.explanation: A producer decrease can reduce food for herbivores.

questions.prompt: A student says, "A population always grows if no predators are present." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "A population always grows if no predators are present." Which correction is best?
options: Food, water, space, disease, and other factors can also limit growth.
questions.correctAnswer: Food, water, space, disease, and other factors can also limit growth.
questions.explanation: Many factors can limit population size.

questions.prompt: A graph shows a population rising quickly, then leveling off. Which explanation is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A graph shows a population rising quickly, then leveling off. Which explanation is most reasonable?
options: The graph proves resources are unlimited.
The population may be approaching a resource limit.
questions.correctAnswer: The population may be approaching a resource limit.
questions.explanation: Leveling off can suggest carrying capacity or resource limits.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows a ripple effect?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows a ripple effect?
options: plants -> no consumers -> no food web
drought -> fewer plants -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds
questions.correctAnswer: drought -> fewer plants -> fewer insects -> fewer insect-eating birds
questions.explanation: A change can ripple through connected populations.

questions.prompt: Which evidence supports that a predator affected a prey population?
questions.questionText: Which evidence supports that a predator affected a prey population?
options: The predator has a short name.
Prey numbers dropped after predator numbers increased, while food supply stayed similar.
questions.correctAnswer: Prey numbers dropped after predator numbers increased, while food supply stayed similar.
questions.explanation: A timing pattern with food controlled can support a predator effect.

questions.prompt: A lake receives extra nutrients, algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. Which factor directly stresses fish?
questions.questionText: A lake receives extra nutrients, algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. Which factor directly stresses fish?
questions.correctAnswer: lower dissolved oxygen
questions.explanation: Fish need dissolved oxygen, so low oxygen can stress them.

questions.prompt: Which investigation best tests whether food limits a population?
questions.questionText: Which investigation best tests whether food limits a population?
options: Compare population growth in similar habitats with different food amounts.
Use habitats that differ in every possible way.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare population growth in similar habitats with different food amounts.
questions.explanation: A fair comparison changes food while keeping other factors similar.

questions.prompt: What does biodiversity often add to ecosystem stability?
questions.questionText: What does biodiversity often add to ecosystem stability?
options: alternative roles and resources when one population changes
questions.correctAnswer: alternative roles and resources when one population changes
questions.explanation: Diversity can provide backup interactions and resources.

questions.prompt: A student sees two populations rising together and claims one caused the other. What should they ask?
questions.questionText: A student sees two populations rising together and claims one caused the other. What should they ask?
options: Can the graph be printed larger?
Is there evidence of a direct interaction or another factor affecting both?
questions.correctAnswer: Is there evidence of a direct interaction or another factor affecting both?
questions.explanation: Correlation alone does not prove cause.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern could show predator-prey cycling?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern could show predator-prey cycling?
options: prey increases, predator increases later, prey decreases, predator decreases later
the graph has no axis labels
questions.correctAnswer: prey increases, predator increases later, prey decreases, predator decreases later
questions.explanation: Predator and prey populations can affect each other with time delays.

questions.prompt: A habitat corridor connects two separated forest patches. Which population effect might it support?
questions.questionText: A habitat corridor connects two separated forest patches. Which population effect might it support?
options: organisms can move between patches more easily
questions.correctAnswer: organisms can move between patches more easily
questions.explanation: Corridors can increase movement between habitat patches.

questions.prompt: Which model revision improves: pollution -> population decrease?
questions.questionText: Which model revision improves: pollution -> population decrease?
options: pollution -> water quality change -> lower survival or resources -> population decrease
pollution -> organisms choose to leave data
questions.correctAnswer: pollution -> water quality change -> lower survival or resources -> population decrease
questions.explanation: A stronger model names the mechanism connecting cause and effect.

questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported if plant cover decreases and soil temperature rises?
questions.questionText: Which claim is best supported if plant cover decreases and soil temperature rises?
options: Plant cover is unrelated to ecosystems.
Plant cover may help regulate habitat conditions.
questions.correctAnswer: Plant cover may help regulate habitat conditions.
questions.explanation: Plant cover can influence shade and soil temperature.

questions.prompt: A population grows beyond available food. Which outcome is likely?
questions.questionText: A population grows beyond available food. Which outcome is likely?
options: survival or growth may decrease as competition increases
questions.correctAnswer: survival or growth may decrease as competition increases
questions.explanation: Resource limits can reduce survival or growth.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken the claim that drought caused a population decline?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken the claim that drought caused a population decline?
options: The population declined before the drought and food availability stayed high.
questions.correctAnswer: The population declined before the drought and food availability stayed high.
questions.explanation: Timing and unchanged resources can weaken a drought-cause claim.

questions.prompt: A graph shows stable total plant cover even after one species decreases because other species increase. What idea does this support?
questions.questionText: A graph shows stable total plant cover even after one species decreases because other species increase. What idea does this support?
options: plants are not part of ecosystems
biodiversity can support stability through replacement roles
questions.correctAnswer: biodiversity can support stability through replacement roles
questions.explanation: Other species can partly maintain ecosystem function.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates whether an ecosystem is resilient after a disturbance?
questions.questionText: Which question best evaluates whether an ecosystem is resilient after a disturbance?
options: Is the graph printed in color?
Do key populations and functions recover over time?
questions.correctAnswer: Do key populations and functions recover over time?
questions.explanation: Resilience is about recovery of populations and functions.

questions.prompt: A food web model has arrows but no population data. What can it show, and what can it not show?
questions.questionText: A food web model has arrows but no population data. What can it show, and what can it not show?
options: It can show feeding relationships, but not how population sizes changed.
questions.correctAnswer: It can show feeding relationships, but not how population sizes changed.
questions.explanation: Food webs show relationships; population data show changes over time.

questions.prompt: Why might removing one predator increase some prey but decrease certain plants?
questions.questionText: Why might removing one predator increase some prey but decrease certain plants?
options: More prey may eat more plants, creating an indirect effect.
questions.correctAnswer: More prey may eat more plants, creating an indirect effect.
questions.explanation: Food-web changes can ripple indirectly.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best shows a resource limit rather than predation?
questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows a resource limit rather than predation?
options: A fossil is found in rock.
Seedlings grow poorly when light is reduced by dense shade.
questions.correctAnswer: Seedlings grow poorly when light is reduced by dense shade.
questions.explanation: Light is a resource for plants; reduced light can limit growth.

questions.prompt: A student claims ecosystem stability means nothing changes. What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student claims ecosystem stability means nothing changes. What is the best correction?
options: Stability means every organism count is identical forever.
Only nonliving systems can be stable.
Stable ecosystems can change but keep key functions within a workable range.
questions.correctAnswer: Stable ecosystems can change but keep key functions within a workable range.
questions.explanation: Stability does not mean no change; it means maintaining functions or recovering.

questions.prompt: Which data would best compare two ecosystems' stability?
questions.questionText: Which data would best compare two ecosystems' stability?
options: population and resource measurements before, during, and after a disturbance
the number of letters in each species name
questions.correctAnswer: population and resource measurements before, during, and after a disturbance
questions.explanation: Stability is best judged across time and disturbance.

questions.prompt: A model predicts fish will recover if stream shade is restored. Which evidence would test the model?
questions.questionText: A model predicts fish will recover if stream shade is restored. Which evidence would test the model?
options: the color of the restoration sign
water temperature, oxygen levels, and fish counts after restoration
the number of rocks in a drawing
questions.correctAnswer: water temperature, oxygen levels, and fish counts after restoration
questions.explanation: The evidence measures the mechanism and outcome.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects population dynamics to energy flow?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects population dynamics to energy flow?
options: Energy flow is unrelated to organisms.
Population changes can alter how much energy moves through feeding relationships.
questions.correctAnswer: Population changes can alter how much energy moves through feeding relationships.
questions.explanation: Feeding relationships transfer energy, so population changes affect transfer patterns.

questions.prompt: A population of algae grows rapidly after nutrients enter a pond. Which later outcome would be important to monitor?
questions.questionText: A population of algae grows rapidly after nutrients enter a pond. Which later outcome would be important to monitor?
options: the spelling of the pond name
dissolved oxygen levels and populations that need oxygen
questions.correctAnswer: dissolved oxygen levels and populations that need oxygen
questions.explanation: Algae blooms can affect oxygen and other populations.

questions.prompt: Which final summary best shows ecosystem data reasoning?
questions.questionText: Which final summary best shows ecosystem data reasoning?
options: Population patterns, resource limits, and food-web models help explain how changes ripple and whether ecosystems remain stable.
One data point proves every cause.
Food webs show exact population size.
Stability means no changes ever occur.
questions.correctAnswer: Population patterns, resource limits, and food-web models help explain how changes ripple and whether ecosystems remain stable.
questions.explanation: This connects data, resources, food webs, ripple effects, and stability.

questions.prompt: Which question makes a student think beyond naming interactions?
questions.questionText: Which question makes a student think beyond naming interactions?
options: What evidence would show whether this interaction changed the population over time?
Can the graph use blue ink?
questions.correctAnswer: What evidence would show whether this interaction changed the population over time?
questions.explanation: Evidence over time is needed to connect interactions to population change.
